title: Leave the phone behind
easy: Walk to the nearest shop or bus stop without your phone.
medium: Run one real errand on foot today with the phone left at home.
brave: Get somewhere you have never been with a paper map or by asking people for directions. Phone stays home.
indoor: Leave the phone in another room for the whole evening meal and the washing up after it.
why: You managed without it for most of history. You can manage for an hour.
pen: Write sentences that begin with "Right now I notice..." for two minutes.

title: Ask a real question
easy: Ask a cashier, driver or neighbour how their day is going, and wait for the real answer.
medium: Ask a friend or family member: "What is taking most of your energy lately?" Then only listen.
brave: Ask someone you trust: "What is one thing I could do better as a friend?" Thank them. Do not defend yourself.
indoor: Call someone and ask what they are looking forward to this month.
why: Most people are rarely asked. Listening is something you can give today.
pen: Write what they said. Then write what you assumed before they said it. Keep the two apart.

title: Plan tomorrow on paper
easy: Tonight, write tomorrow's three most important things on paper.
medium: Write your whole plan for tomorrow on paper, and do not open the calendar app to check it.
brave: Tomorrow, no phone until your first important thing is done. Tell someone, so they know why you are quiet.
indoor: Write tomorrow's plan on paper and put it where you will see it first in the morning.
why: Whoever gets your first hour shapes the rest of the day. Let it be you.
pen: Write three sentences that start with "I have to". Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Listen properly
easy: Next time someone talks to you, put the phone face down and look at them until they finish.
medium: Go through one whole conversation without interrupting. Ask one follow-up question before you say anything about yourself.
brave: In a disagreement today, repeat the other person's point in your own words until they say "yes, that's it". Only then answer.
indoor: Listen to a whole album with your eyes closed, doing nothing else.
why: Observation comes before interpretation. Most of us skip the first part.
pen: Write what they said. Then write what you were thinking while they said it.

title: Choose a small discomfort
easy: End today's shower with cold water, for as long as you can stand it.
medium: No sweets and no snacks between meals today.
brave: Go for a run in the rain or the cold, dressed for it, and finish the route you planned.
indoor: Hold a wall sit until it burns. Then hold it for three more breaths.
why: Practising small discomfort makes larger discomfort less frightening.
pen: Make two columns: what was up to me today, and what was not.

title: Draw what is in front of you
easy: Draw the object nearest to you. No erasing.
medium: Sit somewhere public and sketch a scene with people in it.
brave: Make something by hand, a card, a drawing or a small object, and give it to someone in person today.
indoor: Draw your room from where you are sitting.
why: Drawing forces you to look. Your hands do not scroll.
pen: Write what went well today, what didn't, and what you will do differently tomorrow.

title: Find the horizon
easy: Step outside and find the furthest thing you can see. Look at it properly.
medium: Lie on the grass or a bench and watch the clouds or the stars, phone in your pocket.
brave: Be outside for today's sunset, or tomorrow's sunrise, from start to finish.
indoor: Find the window with the widest view and look out of it for the length of one song.
why: The sky is large and your worries are small. Both are true.
pen: Describe today as if you were watching it from very high above. Keep it short.

title: Thank someone specifically
easy: Thank someone in person for one specific thing they did, and say what it changed for you.
medium: Write a short thank-you note by hand and give it, or leave it where they will find it.
brave: Call or visit someone who helped you years ago, a teacher, a coach, an old boss, and tell them.
indoor: Send a voice message thanking someone for one specific thing.
why: Gratitude said out loud is different from gratitude you only feel.
pen: Write an unsent letter of a few lines to someone who helped you once.

title: One thing at a time
easy: Turn on Do Not Disturb for your next task, and finish the task before you turn it off.
medium: Leave the phone in another room while you work or study for a whole morning or afternoon.
brave: Tell the people who usually reach you that you are offline tonight. Then turn the phone off after dinner.
indoor: Watch one film or episode with the phone in another room.
why: Doing one thing fully is rare now. That makes it worth practising.
pen: Write what happened when you felt the urge to check. Then write what you told yourself about it.

title: Find something new on a known path
easy: On a route you use today, find three things you never noticed before.
medium: Take a different route home today, even if it is slower.
brave: Ask someone who has lived near you for a long time what used to be here. Then go and see the place.
indoor: Find five things at home you have stopped seeing. Clean, move or give away one of them.
why: Habit makes us blind. Attention gives the world back.
pen: For two minutes, write sentences that begin with "Right now I notice..."

title: Use your body on purpose
easy: Take every staircase you meet today. No lifts, no escalators.
medium: Walk or cycle somewhere you would normally drive or ride to.
brave: Join a group class, a run club or a pickup game you have never tried.
indoor: Do twenty squats, ten push-ups, on your knees if you like, and a slow stretch.
why: Action comes before motivation. Move first, and the mood follows.
pen: Write three "I have to" sentences about your body. Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Send something on paper
easy: Write a postcard by hand and post it today.
medium: Write a one-page letter to someone you care about, and post it.
brave: Write to someone you lost touch with or fell out with. Keep it simple, and send it.
indoor: Write a note by hand and leave it where someone at home will find it.
why: A letter takes time to write, which is exactly why it matters.
pen: Write what you wanted to say in the letter but left out, and why you left it out.

title: Spend time with a tree
easy: Stop at a tree on your way today and put your hand on its bark.
medium: Eat your lunch or drink your coffee sitting under a tree.
brave: Plant something outside: a tree, a bulb, seeds in a pot. Or join a local planting or clean-up.
indoor: Repot a plant, or put a seed in a glass of water on the windowsill.
why: Trees grow slowly and do not hurry. You can borrow that.
pen: Make two columns: what is up to me this week, and what is not.

title: Share a meal
easy: Eat one meal today at a table with someone, phones off the table.
medium: Invite someone for a meal or a walk this week, and fix the day and time now.
brave: Invite a neighbour or colleague you barely know for coffee.
indoor: Call someone who lives far away and share a meal over the phone.
why: Shared meals are one of the oldest ways people stay close.
pen: Write what went well in the conversation, what didn't, and what you would do next time.

title: Make the phone boring
easy: Switch your phone to greyscale for the rest of the day.
medium: Move every social and news app off your home screen into one folder on the last page.
brave: Delete the app you open most without thinking. You can install it again next week, if you choose.
indoor: Turn off every notification that does not come from a person.
why: Your phone is designed to pull at you. You can change the design.
pen: Write the facts about how you used your phone today. Then write your judgment about it. Keep them apart.

title: Look closer
easy: Pick one colour and find it five times on your way today.
medium: Stop at one shop window, garden or market stall, and look until you see something you would have missed.
brave: Ask a stranger about what they are doing or making: a gardener, a busker, a stall holder. Then listen.
indoor: Find every shade of one colour in your home.
why: Looking closely is a skill. Skills grow with practice.
pen: Describe one ordinary thing you saw today in so much detail that a stranger could draw it.

title: Breathe before you answer
easy: Before your next meal, take ten slow breaths: four in, six out.
medium: When you feel annoyed today, take three slow breaths before you answer.
brave: Do the task or conversation you have been putting off. Breathe slowly for one minute first, then start right away.
indoor: Lie on the floor with a hand on your belly and breathe slowly for five minutes.
why: Your breath is one of the few things fully up to you.
pen: For two minutes, write sentences that begin with "Right now I notice..."

title: Fix one broken thing
easy: Fix one small thing: a loose button, a squeaky hinge, a wobbly chair.
medium: Repair something you were going to throw away or replace.
brave: Learn to fix something you usually pay for, a bike tyre, a dripping tap, a hem. Ask someone to show you.
indoor: Empty one drawer or shelf completely. Keep what you use and give the rest away.
why: Repair is patient work. It teaches care for what you already have.
pen: Write three "I have to" sentences about your home. Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Go somewhere new nearby
easy: Walk down one street you have never walked down.
medium: Go inside a place near you that you have never entered: a library, a gallery, a cafe, a park.
brave: Take a bus or train to a district or town you have never visited, and find your way around without the phone's map.
indoor: Rearrange one room so it feels like a new place.
why: Small novelty wakes up attention without needing anything big.
pen: Describe today's new place as if you were seeing your whole town from a hill far away.

title: Call instead of text
easy: Answer one message today with a call instead.
medium: Call a friend you have not spoken to in over a month, just to ask how they are.
brave: Call someone with whom something was left unfinished, and say the thing you did not say. Keep it simple.
indoor: Reply to your next message with a voice message instead of typing.
why: A voice carries what text cannot.
pen: Write an unsent letter of a few lines to someone you miss.

title: Leave a moment empty
easy: Next time you wait in a line or for a bus, keep the phone in your pocket.
medium: Go to and from wherever you go today with no headphones.
brave: Go to a cafe or a park alone, without phone, book or music, and stay until you finish a drink.
indoor: Make a cup of tea and sit by a window with nothing in your hands until you finish it.
why: Boredom is where your own thoughts get room to speak.
pen: Write what you thought about when there was nothing to fill the time.

title: Taste your food
easy: Eat the first five bites of one meal slowly, with no screen, noticing taste and texture.
medium: Eat one whole meal today with no screen, book or phone on the table.
brave: Ask the person who made your food how they made it: a cook, a baker, a parent.
indoor: Make a cup of tea or coffee by hand and drink it with nothing else to do.
why: Your body notices what your mind skips over.
pen: Write the facts of one moment today. Then write what you told yourself about it.

title: Move outdoors
easy: Spend your next break walking outside instead of sitting with your phone.
medium: Get your heart rate up outside: a brisk walk, a run or a bike ride, until you sweat.
brave: Climb the highest hill or tower you can reach on foot nearby.
indoor: Dance to three songs with the door closed.
why: The body is not a vehicle for the head. Treat it like a companion.
pen: Write what went well in your body today, what didn't, and what you will try tomorrow.

title: Write one page
easy: Write five lines about a memory from childhood.
medium: Write one page by hand about anything. Do not stop to correct.
brave: Write something short, a poem, a story, a letter, and read it out loud to someone.
indoor: Copy a passage you love by hand, slowly.
why: Writing by hand slows thinking down enough to see it.
pen: Write a few lines to your future self, one year from today. Do not send it anywhere.

title: Go out in any weather
easy: Step outside now, whatever the weather, and stand in it for a minute.
medium: Walk somewhere today in weather you would normally avoid.
brave: Spend an afternoon outside in rough weather, dressed for it: a hike, a long walk, a ride.
indoor: Open the windows wide for ten minutes and air the whole home.
why: The weather is not up to you. How you meet it is.
pen: Make two columns: what was up to me today, and what was not.

title: Help without being asked
easy: Do one helpful thing for someone today without mentioning it.
medium: Offer help to someone who is clearly struggling: carry a bag, hold a door, explain the way.
brave: Sign up to volunteer once this month, at a food bank, a shelter or a clean-up. Do the sign-up today.
indoor: Do a household job that is usually someone else's.
why: Acting for others is one of the surest ways out of your own head.
pen: Write what you did. Then write what you hoped it would mean. Keep them apart.

title: A day without feeds
easy: No social feeds before lunch.
medium: Log out of every social app on your phone. Logging back in takes effort, which is the point.
brave: Take a full day off feeds, and tell one person, so it is real.
indoor: Replace tonight's scroll with a book or a paper.
why: A feed never ends. Your day does. Choose what fills it.
pen: Write three "I have to check" sentences. Rewrite each as "I choose to" or "I won't".

title: Watch one living thing
easy: Stop and watch one bird, insect or animal until it moves away.
medium: Learn the name of one bird or plant you see often, and one true fact about it.
brave: Offer to walk a neighbour's or friend's dog, or help out at an animal shelter.
indoor: Water a plant and look at it closely. Find one new leaf or bud.
why: Patience is learned by watching things that do not hurry.
pen: Describe your life this week as if you were that small creature looking up at it.

title: Protect your sleep
easy: Start getting ready for bed half an hour earlier tonight.
medium: No screens in the last hour before sleep. Read, talk or stretch instead.
brave: Charge the phone outside the bedroom tonight, and every night this week.
indoor: Read on paper for twenty minutes before sleep.
why: Tomorrow's patience is decided partly by tonight's sleep.
pen: Write what went well today, what didn't, and what you will do differently tomorrow.

title: Cook from scratch
easy: Make one meal today from raw ingredients, not from a packet.
medium: Cook a recipe you have never made, from a book or a written recipe.
brave: Cook for at least two other people, and eat together.
indoor: Make something that needs your hands in the dough: bread, pasta, dumplings.
why: What you make carries your time in it. People can taste that.
pen: Write what went well in the cooking, what didn't, and what you would change next time.
